q: How do I calculate PUE for a server room or data centre?
title: PUE formula for a server room
short: Divide the total energy used by the server room or data centre by the energy used by the IT equipment alone, over the same period, ideally a full year. PUE = total facility kWh / IT equipment kWh. A result of 1.0 is the floor; the further above it, the more goes to cooling and losses.
audience: IT and facility teams in India

ul: Total facility energy: everything serving the room, including IT load, cooling, UPS and transformer losses, lighting and any diesel generator output. ISO/IEC 30134-2 counts all energy sources, not only grid power.
IT equipment energy: servers, storage and network gear. Measure it at the UPS output, the PDU output or the equipment input; the further downstream you measure, the more accurate the figure.
Period: use 12 months. A single summer day or the design figure from the vendor will not match your annual result.

sections.h: Measuring it in an Indian office or factory
ol: Fit a sub-meter on the feeder to the server room and its precision air conditioning, or use the incomer meter if the building is a dedicated data centre.
Read the IT load from the UPS output meter or smart PDUs.
If a DG set runs during outages, add its kWh from the DG energy meter to the total.
Record both meters on the same dates each month and add up 12 months.

p: ISO/IEC 30134-2 sets measurement categories by where IT energy is metered: category 1 at the UPS output, category 2 at the PDU output and category 3 at the IT equipment input. Always state the category with the number. Compare your PUE with your own past years rather than a published average from a different climate or size of site.
PUE does not measure whether the servers themselves are efficient. Consolidating idle servers cuts IT kWh and can make PUE look worse even though total energy falls, so track total kWh too.

Emissions come from total facility energy, not from PUE. Multiply the grid kWh in that total by 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, the CEA weighted average factor for India, and for generator output use diesel litres times 2.68 kg CO2 per litre instead of the grid factor. PUE then tells you how much of that is overhead you can cut.

example.title: Worked example: one year for a 35 kW server room
lines: Emissions = 510,000 x 0.710 = 362,100 kg CO2, about 362 tonnes
If cooling changes bring PUE to 1.50: 300,000 x 1.50 = 450,000 kWh, saving 60,000 kWh
Saving = 60,000 x 0.710 = 42,600 kg CO2, about 43 tonnes a year
example.note: Figures are illustrative. Grid electricity only; add generator fuel separately if the DG set ran.
